name: Enhanced matching (hashed email from the browser)
plain: The tag hashes an email address in the browser and sends the hash to LinkedIn to match a member.
meaning: Turns an anonymous visitor into a known LinkedIn member when their email is on the advertiser's form. SHA-256 is deterministic, so the hash is still an identifier.

web.api: Insight Tag enhanced matching: SHA-256 of normalized email

steps: Visitor enters an email on the advertiser's site
Tag lowercases and hashes it with SHA-256
Hash sent to LinkedIn and matched to a member

limits.headline: Can send a scrambled version of your email to LinkedIn to match you to a member
limits.user_action: You type or autofill your email on a site that uses the LinkedIn tag
can: Turn your email into a scrambled code in the browser
Send that code to LinkedIn to find a matching member
Improve how conversions and audiences are matched
cannot: Send the plain email address, only the scrambled code
Match you if LinkedIn has no account using that email
Work if the tag is blocked or you never enter an email
See emails typed on sites without the tag

story.what_it_is: The tag scrambles an email you type and sends the scramble to LinkedIn so it can find your profile.

marketing.name: Enhanced matching
marketing.pitch: LinkedIn presents it as a way for advertisers to improve match rates by sending hashed email from forms on their sites.

story.for_you: You type your email into a form and nothing seems different. Behind the scenes, the page turns your email into a code and sends it to LinkedIn. LinkedIn can then tell which of its members you are.
story.for_makers: Cookies alone miss many visitors. Matching an email to a member makes an anonymous form fill a known lead. That helps advertisers measure sales and build audiences, and it lifts how much LinkedIn can charge.

use_cases.example: You download a white paper with your work email. The advertiser can then show you follow up ads on LinkedIn, tied to that email.
A marketing team sees that a signup came from a LinkedIn ad, even though you used a different browser than the one you clicked in.
A software firm builds a list of people who requested a demo, so it can send ads to their coworkers too.
A course seller matches a purchase email to a LinkedIn member to check the sale came from a paid post.
A scrambled email is stable, so anyone who has your email can compute the same code and match you, which is why it is not anonymous.
A business school ties a brochure request to a LinkedIn profile, to find more people with similar jobs.

risks: Hashed email is still an identifier
Happens before you press submit in some setups

technical_bounds: Needs a form or data layer with the email
Matches only if LinkedIn knows the email

linkedin.how: Per LinkedIn help pages the Insight Tag hashes emails in the browser (summary of pages; marked docs).
